## Review Follow-Up (2026-10-01)

Current head: `635f9cd2eb55403dca8280235dd6e1271cf7c139`. Rebased stack onto upstream `ccda9098cc5a91b6b6f73e0c0e697022382e01b4`.

Narrowed SlidingWindowMLASpec merge validation to `cache_dtype` and `kv_quant_mode`, with separate mismatch regression cases. Upstream DCP metadata is preserved.

[Current incremental diff](https://github.com/meenchen/vllm/compare/ccda9098cc5a91b6b6f73e0c0e697022382e01b4...635f9cd2eb55403dca8280235dd6e1271cf7c139): 6 files changed, 175 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-).

Validation on this head:
- All applicable repository pre-commit hooks passed on the incremental diff, including mypy for Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.
- CPU source-isolated checks passed: 4 existing merge-test cases, 2 additional merge regressions, and 36 dtype-resolver cases. These execute the source definitions with unrelated runtime imports isolated, not the full vLLM test environment.
- `git diff --check` and the credential audit passed.
- GPU/E2E tests were not rerun for this rebase. Earlier GPU results below remain historical evidence for their stated heads, not this head.

Hook command (from this branch):

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref ccda9098cc5a91b6b6f73e0c0e697022382e01b4 --to-ref 635f9cd2eb55403dca8280235dd6e1271cf7c139 --hook-stage manual
```

---

## Purpose

This is the first change in the layer-wise mixed KV-cache stack. It preserves a
layer's logical KV-cache encoding independently of its physical storage dtype
and allocation layout.

This PR:

- adds `AttentionSpec.cache_dtype`;
- populates it from `Attention.get_kv_cache_spec()`;
- adds the generic `QuantizationConfig.get_kv_cache_dtype(prefix)` hook;
- preserves `cache_dtype` and `kv_quant_mode` through full-attention, MLA,
  sliding-window MLA, sink, and recurrent-sliding-window merges; and
- makes FlashInfer resolve KV dtype as explicit global override, then per-spec
  dtype, and reject an ambiguous quantized spec.

This PR does not parse ModelOpt layer-wise metadata or enable heterogeneous KV
allocation. It preserves metadata during merges and adds validation for ambiguous
quantized specs; existing explicitly configured global BF16, FP8, and NVFP4
paths retain their dtype selection.

This change is the first prerequisite for #56116.

This contribution was developed with AI assistance. The human submitter
reviewed the complete diff and remains responsible for the implementation and
validation.

## Review Scope

[Incremental diff](https://github.com/meenchen/vllm/compare/ccda9098cc5a91b6b6f73e0c0e697022382e01b4...635f9cd2eb55403dca8280235dd6e1271cf7c139): 6 files changed, 175 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-).
This PR is the first prerequisite; review and merge it before #56156 and #56116.
The prerequisite branches live in `meenchen/vllm`, so the upstream PRs remain
based on `main`. Descendants will be rebased onto upstream `main` after each
prerequisite merges. These PRs split the former combined #56116 implementation;
their incremental changes do not duplicate one another.

## Test Plan

- Verify full-attention, MLA, and sliding-window MLA merges preserve the logical
  dtype and reject incompatible formats.
- Verify FlashInfer uses a per-spec dtype when the global dtype is `auto`.
- Verify an explicit global dtype takes precedence.
- Verify ambiguous quantized specs fail clearly.

## Test Results

### Mypy Follow-Up

Previously checked head: `3ce9e426db74e36c10b8ac528e3b6da0298e422b`.
The shared fix in `3ce9e426db` replaces tuple-membership narrowing with an
explicit `is not None` guard in FlashInfer's logical-dtype resolver. The
ambiguous-spec test now covers both `None` and `"auto"`.

- Upstream full [pre-commit CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/35185252793)
  **passed** on `3ce9e426db`.
- Repository mypy hook (mypy 1.20.2): Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 targets
  pass on each PR's incremental changed Python files (12 successful checks).
- CPU-only checks execute the source-extracted resolver: 36 cases per branch
  preserve outputs/errors and explicit-global precedence.
- Scoped lint, formatting, repository hooks, and documentation checks pass.
- This behavior-preserving typing fix did not rerun the GPU suites below;
  their recorded tested heads remain unchanged.

### Rebase Validation (2026-09-16)

- Rebased onto upstream `fbf2c5e8be9754f31c4e0f549189fc9f3bdd213c`.
- Tested head: `016f06f4155bf5facca70269bc31cab6e1b90d28`.
- Full `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: **119 passed**.
- FlashInfer logical dtype and single-token XQA CUDA-graph padding tests: **6 passed**.
- AGA job `767402`, GB300, driver `580.167.08`.
- Runtime: vLLM nightly `0.29.1rc1.dev187+gaf1c01499`, PyTorch
  `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.18.post1`.
- Exact branch Python source with installed nightly native extensions and
  wheel-assembled FlashMLA interface files. Source-file hashes were checked
  against the rebased commits. This is not a full source build.
- All feature changes remain Python-only; no extension ABI changes were added.
- Rebase conflicts retained both upstream and PR tests. The feature's production
  patch is unchanged, as checked with `git range-diff`.
- GPU processes were empty after testing; the allocation was released.

### Historical Validation

The pre-rebase logical-dtype suite passed 8 tests on GB300 (job `692321`).
The results above are the fresh tests for this rebased head.

### Local Checks

Previously checked head `3ce9e426db74e36c10b8ac528e3b6da0298e422b` against incremental base
`fbf2c5e8be9754f31c4e0f549189fc9f3bdd213c`:

- Ruff 0.14.0 lint and formatting: passed on every changed Python file.
- Repository hooks for SPDX headers, root lazy imports, forbidden imports,
  torch.cuda calls, config field validation, and boolean context managers: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Reproduce the Ruff checks from this branch:

```bash
git diff --name-only fbf2c5e8be9754f31c4e0f549189fc9f3bdd213c HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs uv tool run --from ruff==0.14.0 ruff check
git diff --name-only fbf2c5e8be9754f31c4e0f549189fc9f3bdd213c HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs uv tool run --from ruff==0.14.0 ruff format --check
```

These are scoped local checks, not a completed full pre-commit or mypy CI run.
The upstream CI contributor-authorization gate has not been bypassed.

@LucasWilkinson Agreed ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56155#pullrequestreview-5475374302)). I added `cache_dtype` because FlashInfer currently reads the global cache dtype, which cannot describe layer-wise FP8/NVFP4. However, each attention layer already owns its resolved `kv_cache_dtype`.

I'll remove the new logical-dtype field from allocation specs, resolve the format from the layers during attention metadata initialization, and distinguish incompatible formats in runtime attention grouping and metadata-reuse keys. why the new assert?

This was intended to prevent merging different logical KV formats while silently retaining the first spec's dtype. Agreed that checking every AttentionSpec field was broader than necessary: narrowed it to `cache_dtype` and `kv_quant_mode` in 635f9cd2eb, with separate mismatch regression cases. hmmm do we have to feed this info through the spec? I think ideally we'd like to move towards the spec just primarily describing the physical allocation so theres less abstraction leakage with the KVCacheManager which should primarily be a memory allocator

Agreed that checking every AttentionSpec field was broader than necessary: narrowed it to `cache_dtype` and `kv_quant_mode` in 635f9cd2eb, with separate mismatch regression cases. Existing validation for other fields is unchanged. Scoped pre-commit (including all four mypy targets) and source-isolated CPU regression checks pass; no fresh GPU pass is claimed.

@LucasWilkinson Agreed ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56155#pullrequestreview-5475374302)). I added `cache_dtype` because FlashInfer currently reads the global cache dtype, which cannot describe layer-wise FP8/NVFP4. However, each attention layer already owns its resolved `kv_cache_dtype`.

I'll remove the new logical-dtype field from allocation specs, resolve the format from the layers during attention metadata initialization, and distinguish incompatible formats in runtime attention grouping and metadata-reuse keys. The specs will retain physical sizing/layout information, with packed allocation handled separately. This is startup bookkeeping, not additional per-token synchronization.
